- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak or mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.8 in 3 days), model fails to adjust quickly; apply “sentiment pivot” — shift forecast mean toward sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–3% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; for 30d, apply “sentiment decay” — weight recent sentiment (last 5 days) 70%, prior 30% to dampen overfitting.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; add 1–2% lagged momentum to forecast if no recent sentiment shift.
